source: CHANGELOG.md 0.1.0 to 0.33.1 and docs/design.md sections 10 to 26

items.label: One jobserver for every build
items.detail: slot serve owns one GNU-make jobserver FIFO; cargo, rustc and GNU make in every job draw from it.

items.label: Queue by priority, then arrival
items.detail: A job waits until the slots it needs are free; jobs are admitted by level (urgent, high, normal, low), in the order they arrived inside a level (0.17.0).

items.label: Cancel a job
items.detail: slot cancel <id> ends a queued or running job of your own; Ctrl-C, SIGTERM or SIGHUP to the client does the same (0.5.1).

items.label: Run-time limit
items.detail: slot run-limit 10m ends a job that runs longer, with exit 124; a job names its own time with slot --timeout or SLOT_TIMEOUT, up to 1 hour unless slot run-limit --max changes it. No limit until one is set. (0.22.0)

items.label: Build processes per job
items.detail: slot job-parallel 4 starts every job with a bound of its own (CARGO_BUILD_JOBS and MAKEFLAGS=-j) in place of the pool's jobserver: compilers take no slots, a freed slot goes to the queue, and the pool limits jobs, not compilers (up to slots x 4 of them). Off until it is set. (0.23.0)

items.label: Waits for disk and memory
items.detail: A job queues while its filesystem has under 25 GB free or available memory is below its expected peak (0.5.0).

items.label: Waits for the host's CPUs
items.detail: slot cpu-limit 17 holds the start of a queued job while the pool's jobs and the compile cache server use 17 or more CPUs and 4 jobs run; work outside both is not counted; a held job starts after 10 minutes at the latest, a job predicted to run 30 s or less is not held (0.26.0), slot cpu-limit --pressure P also holds while CPU pressure is at P % or more (0.27.0). Off until it is set. (0.24.0)

items.label: Short jobs pass long ones
items.detail: Within one level a job predicted to run 5 s or less starts ahead of longer ones, and a request for many slots does not collect every freed slot while the jobs behind it wait; no job is passed for longer than slot serve --pass-for (300 s). (0.25.0)

items.label: Admission by share
items.detail: slot admission shares starts a job while the CPUs its earlier runs used fit a budget measured from the pool and the compile cache; jobs that idle lend their share to the queue. Off until it is set: slot admission slots is the default. (0.25.0)

items.label: The caller's open-file limit
items.detail: A local job runs with the open-file limit of the process that called slot, capped at the daemon's hard limit. (0.25.0)

items.label: Waits for its target directory
items.detail: A cargo build takes no slot while another job of the pool compiles in its target directory; it stays queued with the reason and starts when that job has compiled or ended (0.21.0).

items.label: Frees disk from old target directories
items.detail: Under 40 GB free, the least recently built Cargo target directories that jobs used are deleted until 50 GB are free; the first release only reports what it would delete (0.15.0).

items.label: Upgrade a busy daemon
items.detail: systemctl --user reload slot re-executes at once and hands every running and queued job to the new binary (0.11.0).

items.label: Lost slots come back
items.detail: Tokens a killed compiler took with it are written back within 45 s, also while other builds have the jobserver open; slot status shows how many are missing (0.21.1).

items.label: Job priority
items.detail: slot --priority <level> or SLOT_PRIORITY sets a job's level; slot priority set <repo> <level> keeps rules per repository; a job queued 30 minutes counts as high, a delay slot priority promote-after changes while the daemon runs (0.21.0); an urgent job may borrow slots the headroom holds back (0.17.0).

items.label: Share of the pool
items.detail: slot usage and the web view sum slot time, CPU time, jobs and queue wait per project, repository or session over a window (0.17.0).

items.label: A job names its slots
items.detail: slot --tokens N or SLOT_TOKENS=N holds N slots for a job, for a script that starts a container with --cpus N (0.16.0).

items.label: Disk eviction of local target directories
items.detail: Under the disk floor the daemon deletes the least recently used target directories by default; evict.json in the state directory turns on a dry run without a reload (0.19.0).

items.label: rust, go, node-test, ignite and other
items.detail: cargo is a jobserver client, go holds a fixed share and runs with -p set to it, ignite test holds one slot per test job (0.13.0), anything else holds one slot and passes the pool down.

items.label: Headroom
items.detail: slot headroom N or the web UI slider keeps N % of the CPU out of builds, by slots and by a systemd CPU quota (0.3.0).

items.label: Headroom of the machine
items.detail: slot headroom --base machine: the pool's CPU quota is lowered by the load measured outside it, down to 2 CPUs, so the whole machine stays under the target; status and the web view name the top cgroups outside (0.16.0).

items.label: Call mode
items.detail: While a call uses the microphone or camera, the headroom goes up to the call value and back 2 minutes after (0.5.0).

items.label: Web UI
items.detail: It opens on a cluster view: a card per node with its slots, CPU, memory and free disk, and jobs moving from the queue to their node (0.31.0). The jobs view has four line charts (cores, pressure, pool size, what the compile cache answered per minute), then running, queued and finished jobs, the host census, sessions and a timeline, with live output, on 127.0.0.1:7411 (0.21.0). Jobs name their repository and worktree; the charts keep up to six hours of history across a reload (0.19.1).

items.label: Job log
items.detail: One JSON line per finished job: command, toolchain, slots held, queue wait, run time, CPU seconds, peak memory, exit code.

items.label: sccache watchdog
items.detail: The daemon refills an sccache server jobserver that has leaked its tokens (0.5.0).

items.label: Compile cache record
items.detail: Once a minute the daemon records the hits, misses and refused calls of each running sccache server; a rust job records its cache environment and is warned when it switches the cache off (0.20.0).

items.label: Remote build server
items.detail: SLOT_HOST syncs the repository with rsync and runs the build through slot proxy over ssh; target directories stay on the server.

items.label: Fetch artifacts back
items.detail: slot --fetch PATH copies named build outputs from the server into the checkout after the job exits 0 (0.8.0).

items.label: Target directory seeding and eviction
items.detail: A new worktree starts from a reflink copy of the same repository's latest target directory; least recently used ones are deleted over --cache-budget or the disk floor (0.9.0).

items.label: Restricted ssh command
items.detail: slot shell, an authorized_keys forced command that runs only the sync, fetch, proxy and cancel steps (0.10.0).

items.label: Per-repository configuration
items.detail: .slot.toml lists command prefixes that run on the local daemon while SLOT_HOST sends the rest to the server (0.7.0).

items.label: Claude Code plugin
items.detail: A PreToolUse hook refuses builds outside the pool, also behind shell keywords, timeout and env options and eval (0.19.1); the slot-warden agent lists sessions that bypass it (0.4.0).

items.label: Builds in a sandbox
items.detail: slot gate lets a sandbox with no socket and no network queue its builds in the pool through FIFOs; the build runs in the sandbox (0.18.0).
